title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a Punjabi, use tag questions and emphasis particles, call friends the way they call each other, ask people to repeat or explain, and mix in English the way people really do.
intro:
You can have perfect grammar and still sound like a textbook. What makes Punjabi sound alive are the little words: ਸੱਚੀਂ? 'really?', ਵਾਹ!, ਚੱਲ ਝੂਠਾ!, the ਨਾ at the end of 'you'll come, ਨਾ?', the ਤਾਂ and ਹੀ that carry emphasis, the ਓਏ / ਵੇ / ਨੀ friends use to call each other, and echo words like ਚਾਹ ਸ਼ਾਹ 'tea and stuff'.

This unit also gives you the survival kit every learner needs — 'say that again?', 'slower, please', 'what's this called?', 'what does this word mean?' — and shows how Punjabis slip English into their sentences without breaking the Punjabi grammar.

grammar.title: Tag questions: ਨਾ?, ਹੈ ਨਾ?
grammar.body:
English has a different tag for every sentence — 'isn't it?', 'won't you?', 'didn't they?'. Punjabi mostly uses one tiny word: **ਨਾ**.

**1. Statement + ਨਾ?** = 'right? isn't it? won't you?'. The verb stays exactly as it was: ਤੂੰ ਆਵੇਂਗਾ **ਨਾ**? 'you'll come, won't you?'; ਤੁਸੀਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਹੋ **ਨਾ**? 'you're Punjabi, aren't you?'. A rising voice asks for confirmation; a firm falling voice means 'I'm telling you!'.

**2. ਹੈ ਨਾ?** can be added after any statement, like 'right?'. It is a fixed phrase and does **not** change for past or plural: ਫ਼ਿਲਮ ਵਧੀਆ ਸੀ, **ਹੈ ਨਾ**?; ਉਹ ਬਹੁਤ ਚੰਗੇ ਲੋਕ ਹਨ, **ਹੈ ਨਾ**?

**3. ਨਾ after a command = 'come on, please'**: ਆ ਜਾ **ਨਾ**! 'oh come on, do come!'; ਦੱਸ **ਨਾ**! 'go on, tell me!'. It coaxes and pleads at once.

**4. Position is everything.** ਨਾ **before** the verb means 'don't': **ਨਾ ਦੱਸ** 'don't tell (me)'; **after** it, it coaxes: **ਦੱਸ ਨਾ** 'go on, tell me'.

**5. Other tags**: **ਠੀਕ ਹੈ?** 'OK?', **ਸਹੀ?** 'right?', and among older speakers **ਕਿਉਂ?** or **ਕਿਉਂ ਜੀ?** 'isn't that so?' at the end of an opinion.

Answer a tag question with ਹਾਂ / ਹਾਂ ਜੀ / ਬਿਲਕੁਲ — or, to disagree gently, ਨਹੀਂ ਯਾਰ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਤਾਂ… 'nah, I thought…'.

examples.roman: tūṃ káll pārṭī te āveṅgā nā?
examples.en: You're coming to the party tomorrow, aren't you?
The food was good, wasn't it?

grammar.title: Emphasis with ਹੀ, ਤਾਂ, ਵੀ — and calling people: ਓਏ, ਵੇ, ਨੀ, ਬਈ
grammar.body:
Punjabi puts feeling into small particles placed **right after** the word they affect.

**ਹੀ** (casual and Majhi: **ਈ**) — 'exactly, only, just, very': ਹੁਣੇ ਹੀ 'just now', ਮੈਂ ਹੀ ਕੀਤਾ 'I'm the one who did it', ਪਤਾ ਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ 'had no idea at all'. It fuses with some words: ਇਹ + ਹੀ = **ਇਹੀ** 'this very', ਉਹ + ਹੀ = **ਉਹੀ** 'that same', ਹੁਣ + ਹੀ = **ਹੁਣੇ** 'right now'. **ਤਾਂ ਹੀ** = 'that's why'.

**ਤਾਂ** — contrast and focus, 'as for…, well…, at least': ਮੈਨੂੰ **ਤਾਂ** ਪਸੰਦ ਹੈ 'well, *I* like it'; ਫ਼ਿਲਮ **ਤਾਂ** ਵਧੀਆ ਸੀ 'the film was good (but…)'. After a command it pushes: ਵੇਖ **ਤਾਂ** ਸਹੀ! 'just look!'.

**ਵੀ** — 'also, even': ਉਸ ਨੂੰ **ਵੀ** ਨਹੀਂ ਪਤਾ 'even he doesn't know'; ਕੁਝ ਵੀ 'anything at all', ਕੋਈ ਵੀ 'anyone at all'.

**Calling people** (informal — friends and family only):
• **ਓਏ** — to a boy or man, mostly between male friends
• **ਵੇ** — used by women and girls to a boy or man
• **ਨੀ** — to a girl or woman
• **ਬਈ** — 'well, man', a relaxed filler for anyone
The person called is often in the vocative: ਮੁੰਡਾ → **ਮੁੰਡਿਆ**, ਕੁੜੀ → **ਕੁੜੀਏ**, ਭਰਾ → **ਭਰਾਵਾ**: ਵੇ ਮੁੰਡਿਆ!, ਨੀ ਕੁੜੀਏ!

These are warm with the right people and rude with the wrong ones: ਓਏ to a stranger or an elder can start a fight. With elders, strangers and at work use ਜੀ, ਭਾਜੀ, ਭੈਣ ਜੀ, ਅੰਕਲ ਜੀ.

grammar.title: Echo words, doubling and mixing in English
grammar.body:
**Echo words** turn a noun into 'X and that sort of thing'. Repeat the word with its first consonant replaced by **ਸ਼**: ਚਾਹ → **ਚਾਹ ਸ਼ਾਹ** 'tea or something', ਰੋਟੀ → **ਰੋਟੀ ਸ਼ੋਟੀ** 'a bite to eat', ਕੰਮ → **ਕੰਮ ਸ਼ੰਮ** 'work and stuff'. It's casual and friendly — perfect for invitations. The neutral equivalent is **ਵਗੈਰਾ** 'etc.': ਕੱਪੜੇ, ਜੁੱਤੀਆਂ ਵਗੈਰਾ.

**Doubling** a word changes its meaning:
• question words → 'what all, who all, where all' (asking for a list): **ਕੀ ਕੀ** ਖਾਧਾ? **ਕੌਣ ਕੌਣ** ਆ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ? **ਕਿੱਥੇ ਕਿੱਥੇ** ਗਏ?
• adjectives → warmth, intensity or 'each one': **ਗਰਮ ਗਰਮ** ਰੋਟੀਆਂ 'piping hot rotis', **ਛੋਟੇ ਛੋਟੇ** ਬੱਚੇ 'little kids'
• adverbs → repetition or gradualness: ਹੌਲੀ ਹੌਲੀ 'little by little', ਵਾਰ ਵਾਰ 'again and again'.

**Mixing in English** is normal for young urban Punjabis in India and abroad. The rule is simple: the **content words** may be English, the **grammar** stays Punjabi.
• English verbs come in as a noun or adjective + **ਕਰਨਾ** (when you do something) or **ਹੋਣਾ** (when it happens): ਮੈਂ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਾਲ **ਕਰਦਾ** ਹਾਂ; ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਕੈਂਸਲ **ਹੋ ਗਈ**.
• Postpositions, endings and word order are Punjabi: ਮੇਰੇ ਫ਼ੋਨ **ਦੀ** ਬੈਟਰੀ; ਉਹ ਬਿਜ਼ੀ **ਹੈ**.
• English nouns get a gender, usually by sound or by the Punjabi word they replace: ਮੀਟਿੰਗ (f), ਫ਼ੋਨ (m), ਬੈਟਰੀ (f).

With grandparents, in villages and in formal settings, people switch to **ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ** — and a learner who does the same wins hearts.

culture:
Punjabi conversation is loud, warm and full of reactions — a raised voice and a slap on the back usually mean enthusiasm, not anger. Listeners keep the speaker going with ਅੱਛਾ?, ਹਾਂ ਹਾਂ, ਸੱਚੀਂ?, ਫਿਰ?, and a story without a few ਹਾਏ!s and ਵਾਹ!s falls flat. Famous exclamations: **ਬੱਲੇ ਬੱਲੇ** (celebration) and **ਚੱਕ ਦੇ ਫੱਟੇ** 'go for it!, smash it!'.

The call words ਓਏ, ਵੇ and ਨੀ are the sound of friendship and family; between strangers they are rude. Regional flavour shows in small words: Majhi speakers around Amritsar and Lahore say ਈ for ਹੀ and ਸੀਗਾ for ਸੀ; Malwa speakers say ਆਂ for ਹਾਂ / ਹੈ (ਮੈਂ ਠੀਕ ਆਂ).

Code-mixing is everywhere in cities, on WhatsApp and in songs, and a learner who drops in ਸੀਰੀਅਸਲੀ or ਕੈਂਸਲ won't sound foreign. But Punjabis are delighted by a foreigner who speaks real Punjabi — expect to be tested ('ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ?'), praised (ਮੰਨ ਗਏ!) and then spoken to at full speed. Asking ਹੌਲੀ ਬੋਲੋ ਜੀ or ਇਸ ਦਾ ਕੀ ਮਤਲਬ ਹੈ? is never embarrassing — people love explaining their language.

tip.title: Reacting like a Punjabi
tip.body:
- Surprise: **ਸੱਚੀਂ?** 'really?'; playful disbelief **ਚੱਲ ਝੂਠਾ!** (ਝੂਠੀ to a girl).
- Praise: **ਵਾਹ!**, **ਸ਼ਾਬਾਸ਼!** — but **ਵਾਹ ਜੀ ਵਾਹ!** is usually sarcastic. Annoyance: **ਉਫ਼!**
- Keep the verb agreeing: ਤੂੰ ਲੇਟ **ਆਇਆ** ਹੈਂ (to a boy), **ਆਈ** ਹੈਂ (to a girl).

tip.title: Right?: ਨਾ? and ਹੈ ਨਾ?
tip.body:
- Add **ਨਾ** at the end for 'right? won't you?': ਤੂੰ ਆਵੇਂਗਾ **ਨਾ**? The verb doesn't change.
- **ਹੈ ਨਾ?** after any statement is fixed — even after a past: ਵਧੀਆ ਸੀ, **ਹੈ** ਨਾ?
- After a command ਨਾ coaxes: ਦੱਸ **ਨਾ**! 'go on, tell me!' — but **ਨਾ** ਦੱਸ = 'don't tell'.

tip.title: ਹੀ, ਤਾਂ, ਵੀ — and ਓਏ, ਵੇ, ਨੀ
tip.body:
- **ਹੀ / ਈ** 'just, exactly', **ਤਾਂ** 'well, as for…', **ਵੀ** 'even': they go right **after** the word they stress: ਮੈਨੂੰ **ਤਾਂ** ਪਸੰਦ ਹੈ.
- Calling friends: **ਓਏ** (to a boy, from the boys), **ਵੇ** (to a boy, from a woman), **ਨੀ** (to a girl).
- Only with people you're close to — elders get ਜੀ.
tip.pattern: word + ਹੀ / ਤਾਂ / ਵੀ  ·  ਓਏ / ਵੇ / ਨੀ + name

lessons.title: Say that again?

tip.title: I didn't get it: ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਈ
tip.body:
- Understanding 'comes' to you: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ **ਆਈ** 'I didn't get it', ਹੁਣ ਸਮਝ ਆ **ਗਈ** 'now I get it' — ਸਮਝ is feminine.
- Ask: **ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੀ ਕਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ?** and **ਇਸ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦਾ ਕੀ ਮਤਲਬ ਹੈ?**
- 'Again' = ਫਿਰ ਤੋਂ or ਦੁਬਾਰਾ; 'slower' = ਹੌਲੀ.

lessons.title: Tea-shmea: echo words and keeping it flowing

tip.title: Echo words and doubling
tip.body:
- Echo a noun with **ਸ਼-** for 'and stuff': **ਚਾਹ ਸ਼ਾਹ** 'tea or something', **ਰੋਟੀ ਸ਼ੋਟੀ** 'a bite to eat'. Neutral: **ਵਗੈਰਾ** 'etc.'.
- Double a question word for 'what all / who all': **ਕੀ ਕੀ** ਲਿਆਂਦਾ? **ਕੌਣ ਕੌਣ** ਆਇਆ?
- Double an adjective for warmth or 'each': **ਗਰਮ ਗਰਮ** ਚਾਹ, **ਛੋਟੇ ਛੋਟੇ** ਬੱਚੇ.
tip.pattern: ਚਾਹ ਸ਼ਾਹ  ·  ਕੀ ਕੀ  ·  ਗਰਮ ਗਰਮ

lessons.title: Mixing in English

tip.title: English words, Punjabi grammar
tip.body:
- English verbs come in with **ਕਰਨਾ** (you do it) or **ਹੋਣਾ** (it happens): ਕਾਲ **ਕਰਦਾ** ਹਾਂ, ਕੈਂਸਲ **ਹੋ ਗਈ**.
- Postpositions, endings and word order stay Punjabi: ਫ਼ੋਨ **ਦੀ** ਬੈਟਰੀ, ਬਿਜ਼ੀ **ਹਾਂ**.
- With elders and in the village, mix less: **ਸ਼ੁੱਧ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ** wins hearts.
